name: Simien Mountains National Park
blurb: Geladas, walia ibex and Ethiopian wolves on a high, cliff-edged plateau.

tip.title: Thin the highland grass
tip.text: Grass feeds geladas, walia and the grass rats the Ethiopian wolf lives on. Set Highland grasses to -100% and watch herbivores, then the wolf and leopard.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Simien Mountains National Park, Gelada, Ethiopian wolf). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Strong high-altitude sunlight powers the grasses, heath and lobelia of the plateau, though nights bring frost.
Summer rains and hail feed the highland grasslands that geladas graze; the dry season brings frost and thin forage.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses, returning nutrients to the highland soil.

story: Simien Mountains National Park in northern Ethiopia is the country's largest, covering the highest parts of the range including Ras Dashan, Ethiopia's highest point. It was established in 1969.
matters: It shelters the endangered Ethiopian wolf and walia ibex, a wild goat found nowhere else, along with gelada. People have lived and farmed in the Simien region for at least 2,000 years.
